# Preprocessing log

*Generated by `python -m factcheck.preprocess` (seed 13). Counts are claims unless stated otherwise.*

## 0. Input
- FEVER sample rows in: **3000** ({'SUPPORTS': 1000, 'REFUTES': 1000, 'NOT ENOUGH INFO': 1000})

## 1. Normalization (offset-preserving)
NFKC, PTB escapes (`-LRB-` to `(` and so on), whitespace collapse, and no space before punctuation. Every output character maps back to a raw span, so offsets computed on normalized text can be mapped back to `raw_text`. The raw text is never overwritten.
- claims in: 3000, out: 3000 (normalization drops nothing); claims whose text changed: 5
- example (evidence sentence):
  - before: `Billboard Dad -LRB- film -RRB- is a 1998 American direct-to-video comedy film , directed by Alan Metter starring Mary-Kate and Ashley Olsen .`
  - after: `Billboard Dad (film) is a 1998 American direct-to-video comedy film, directed by Alan Metter starring Mary-Kate and Ashley Olsen.`
- example (claim):
  - before: `198 riders participated in the 2016 Tour  de France.`
  - after: `198 riders participated in the 2016 Tour de France.`

## 2. Claim splitting
Regex sentence splitter that skips abbreviations and single initials. A FEVER claim is already one sentence, so the rows are kept whole. Splitting matters for free text passed to `check()` and to the CLI.
- claims in: 3000, rows with more than one sentence: 0, rows out: 3000
- example (free text): `Paris is in France. Dr. Smith lives there. It has 2.1 million people.` gives `Paris is in France.`, `Dr. Smith lives there.`, `It has 2.1 million people.`

## 3. Opinion filter
Rule-based (first-person stance, evaluative adjectives, `should`), ignoring matches inside capitalized names and titles. Flagged rows stay in the data with `is_opinion=true`. `check()` does not verify them and returns NOT ENOUGH INFO, so any false positive on FEVER counts as an error in the results.
- claims in: 3000, flagged as opinion: 5 (labels: {'REFUTES': 3, 'NOT ENOUGH INFO': 2})
  - flagged: `Global warming is expected to be greatest in the Caribbean.` (gold REFUTES)
  - flagged: `Don Bradman was called the "greatest living Australian" by Margaret Thatcher.` (gold REFUTES)
  - flagged: `A monster is always beautiful.` (gold REFUTES)
  - flagged: `No Country for Old Men was selected as the best of 2007 by the National Board of Review.` (gold NOT ENOUGH INFO)
  - flagged: `Civilization IV was regarded as an amazing product.` (gold NOT ENOUGH INFO)

## 4. De-duplication
Exact hash of the normalized, lowercased claim; then word 3-gram Jaccard of at least 0.9 against the rows already kept, same label only. The first occurrence is kept, and exact duplicates with the same label pass their gold evidence to it (FEVER lists a claim once per evidence set). Near-identical claims with different labels are FEVER mutation pairs and are kept; the split by source keeps each pair on one side.
- claims in: 3000, exact duplicates dropped: 354, near duplicates dropped: 0, out: 2646
- dropped pairs whose labels disagree: 3
  - dropped `Animals are part of the History of Earth.` (SUPPORTS); kept `Animals are part of the History of Earth.` (SUPPORTS)

## 5. Split by source
Whole `source_id` groups (Wikipedia page) are assigned with seed 13 and target ratios 70/15/15. No source appears in two splits.

| split | claims | sources | SUPPORTS | REFUTES | NEI |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| train | 1853 | 669 | 631 | 591 | 631 |
| dev | 397 | 160 | 125 | 140 | 132 |
| test | 396 | 137 | 127 | 123 | 146 |

- source overlap train/dev: 0, train/test: 0, dev/test: 0

## 6. Climate-FEVER (evaluation only)
- rows in: 1381 (after dropping DISPUTED at ingest), flagged opinion: 25, exact duplicates: 1, near duplicates: 29, out: 1351. Everything goes in one evaluation split; nothing is tuned on it.
